 Most recent Most popular 'A point fair', says Buddies boss published at 22:34 GMT 22:34 GMT 
 FT: St Mirren 1-1 Hibernian 
 St Mirren manager Craig McLeish tells BBC Scotland: "Positive that we came away with a point on a night where we probably haven't hit our levels in terms of performance. 
 "I thought defensively we looked solid. Probably not a game that looks exactly how we want it to be but you're going to have nights where you're not quite at it and we've still managed to come away with a point. 
 "The response to going a goal down was excellent and we probably had two or three clear cut chances after that to go and win the game, I think a point is fair for both sides."

 Celtic fail to make most of 'very strong second half' published at 22:32 GMT 22:32 GMT 
 FT: Celtic 2-2 Dundee United 
 Celtic manager Martin O'Neill tells BBC Scotland he believes his side did enough to take all three points.
 "I thought second half we were very, very strong - and yet maybe we could have conceded," he says. "We could have scored a couple of other goals.
 "We fell asleep and conceded the goal, then another one. Half time allowed us to regroup and I thought the second half was very strong."
 Asked if only six clean sheets in 24 games was a concern, O'Neill replies: "You are always going to look at goals you concede and think you can do better. Sometimes we just give the ball away in important positions.
 "In saying that, [Haissem] Hassan has caused havoc in the second half and we should be getting on the end of one or two.
 "I think we just have to move on and it's a big match against Falkirk on Sunday."
 Image source, SNS

 Motherwell 'deserved more' - Johansson published at 22:29 GMT 22:29 GMT 
 FT: St Johnstone 2-2 Motherwell 
 Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson tells BBC Scotland: "It’s an extremely sore end to the game. Obviously, it’s very,
very tough given the fact that I think we played quite a good game and probably
should have scored more than two. To finish it off like that is very tough, it
feels like the story of our performances recently.
 "I think at some point this group of players are going to get
rewarded. We just need to learn from this. In the first half we create chances that we don’t capitalise on and they
score which at that time is difficult. It’s very, very painful at the end.
 "I think we deserved more today but once again I’d say we
need to grow up and learn how to deal with these situations."

 'Not a classic' - McGlynn published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 FT: Aberdeen 0-1 Falkirk 
 Falkirk manager John McGlynn tells BBC Scotland: "Delighted to win. Coming to Aberdeen isn't easy at any time. It wasn't a classic, we've played better and Stephen [Robinson] might say the same.
 "Nothing in the game at all, we rode our luck at times in the second half. But our boys showed a great attitude, they worked exceptionally hard. Ben Krauhaus has taken the goal well.
 "We've won three in a row, which is not easy in the Premiership. Delighted with that. It wasn't pleasing on the eye, we need to pass the ball better, but you take it over the course of a season.
 "We had to battle and we fought, and we've got to give our players credit for that."

 FULL-TIME Dundee 3-1 Kilmarnock published at 21:41 GMT 21:41 GMT 
 Dundee are up to fourth and Kilmarnock slump to the bottom of the table.
 More defensive woes for Neil McCann, who sees his team concede two painful goals in the final seven minutes.
 In fairness, the first of those late salvos was a fantastic header from Ashley Hay, who'd already had a goal ruled out for handball.
 The second, though? Debutant goalkeeper Nico Mantl came racing from his net in bizarre circumstances, allowing Hay to gallop into the box and put into the empty goal.
 Kilmarnock had fought back from Joe Bevan's neat opener when Joe Hugill levelled from the penalty spot, but as they fall back to bottom spot, their ugly 'goals against' figure rises to a league-worst 26.

 At a glance 
 Duran fires Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic in front
 In-form visitors reply with two goals in three minutes by Sapsford and Farrugia 
 Scales equalises after the break as sides share points 
 By Clive Lindsay BBC Sport Scotland Celtic were held to a thrilling draw as Dundee United extended their unbeaten run to six games and the hosts retained their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership. 
 It looked like Jim Goodwin's visitors might end a 34-year, 51-game wait for a win at Celtic Park when goals from Zac Sapsford and Neil Farrugia gave them a half-time lead after Camilo Duran's opener for the hosts.
 But Liam Scales' equaliser ensured Celtic secured a deserved point given their second-half pressure, albeit they have won just three times in their latest nine outings.
 Both sides had gone close from set-pieces before the hosts broke the deadlock - and it was no surprise that it came from Duran.
 Kasper Hogh knocked the ball back into his path inside the box and his Colombian strike partner slotted it home with typical aplomb for this 12th goal of the season.
 Jesse Randall was denied by Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone from close range and Benjamin Nygren by Jack Walton at the other end before the game took an unexpected twist.
 Sapsford, fresh from scoring the weekend winner against Aberdeen, rose in similar fashion to meet a Lyall Cameron free-kick and glance into the far corner.
 Three minutes later, another Cameron free-kick bounced off Bert Esselink into the path of fellow defender Farrugia to prod home his first United goal off the despairing Liam Scales.
 Two half-time changes turned the tide back in Celtic's favour.
 With Hogh and Callum Osmand withdrawn by manager Martin O'Neill and Haissem Hassan and Jota recruited on the wings, the latter's inswinging cross following a corner was glanced inside the far post off the head of Scales.
 Celtic piled on the pressure, but United held on for a point, although that was not enough to prevent Dundee leapfrogging them into fourth.
 Where are Celtic & O'Neill a year after Rodgers exit? 
 Published 1 day ago 
 Johnston faces weeks out but injury 'not too bad' 
 Published 1 day ago 
 Celtic analysis: Hogh and home form a worry 
 O'Neill - looking to celebrate a year in charge with a victory - had stayed loyal to Hogh by naming an unchanged side following Sunday win away to Hibernian.
 It worked initially with the Dane setting up Duran for the opener. However, Hogh failed to threaten to add to his 11 goals this season and was hooked at half-time.
 The introduction of wingers Jota and Haissem Hassan for Callum Osmand and Hogh - with Duran pushed through the middle - turned the game in Celtic's favour.
 However, they were unable to make the pressure count.
 Celtic's nine wins in 11 home league games since the start of March is still more than any other Premiership side and their 23 in 30 this calendar year is also five more than any of their rivals.
 However, despite still being in pole position at the top of the table, a run of one win in their latest five home games will be a concern, albeit their three defeats came against Ferencvaros, Rangers, Celta Vigo.
 Dundee United analysis: Gentleman Jim works magic 
 Much has been made of Goodwin's admission that Jens Berthal Askou's success with Motherwell last season had forced a stylistic rethink and his side are, at times, starting to display a similar swagger.
 O'Neill, who was manager way back when the Irishman was a Celtic youth, also spoke glowingly pre-match of "gentleman" Jim's abilities as a coach.
 Goodwin certainly appears to have got his tactics right as his one change from the weekend win over Aberdeen - Farrugia replacing Daniel Bennie - proved astute as he put United ahead with his first goal for the club in his first start of the season.
 Style was ditched for desperate defending in the second half as they failed to end that Celtic Park hoodoo and relinquished fourth place to city rivals Dundee.
 However, United have now only lost once in their latest four meetings with Celtic - and not many Premiership managers can say that.
